{"id":"project-LICHEN-tb6q.2","title":"Dead code: unpin() and KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED have no valid use","description":"Since IID = hash(pubkey), changing a node's keypair necessarily changes its IID. The concept of 'key rotation for the same IID' is cryptographically impossible without a SHA-256 collision.

Affected code:
1. processor.py:50 - KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED enum value is defined but never used
2. processor.py:253-260 - unpin() method exists but has no valid use case
3. processor.py:245-251 - reset_seen() may also be dead for the same reason

The docstrings and comments reference 'key rotation' which misleads readers into thinking this is possible. The spec section 8.6 describes key rotation with signed handoff (old key signs new key), but that would create a new IID anyway.

What goes wrong: Dead code creates maintenance burden and misleads developers about protocol semantics. The test_unpin_allows_key_rotation test (separate issue) provides false confidence.

Recommendation: Either remove dead code, or document why it exists (e.g., future protocol extension for delegated identity that allows key rotation without IID change).","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-07-06T15:48:35.769783Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-07-06T17:45:23.393537Z","closed_at":"2026-07-06T17:45:23.393537Z","close_reason":"Closed","labels":["owner-reserved","review","risk"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-tb6q.2","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-tb6q","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-07-06T15:48:35.770323Z"}]}

new_value: Removed dead announce-processor code in rust/lichen-node/src/announce.rs: AnnounceProcessor::unpin(), AnnounceProcessor::reset_seen(), and the false-confidence test reset_seen_allows_reaccept. Python twin already removed both methods from processor.py, so removal restores cross-impl parity; KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED itself is not dead on the Rust side (AnnounceRejectReason::KeyChangeDetected is produced on pinned-key mismatch at announce.rs:153, mirroring python KEY_MISMATCH), and no wire format or test/vectors consumer encodes it. Verified: cargo clippy -p lichen-node --all-features -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check -p lichen-node clean; cargo test -p lichen-node --all-features 247/248 - the single failure (rpl_stack::tests::announcement_bootstraps_real_l2_peer_and_rejects_tampering, Receive(SchcDecompress)) is concurrent in-flight work by another session in rpl_stack/schc glue (lichen-schc crate itself passes 100%), on a path that fails before any announce processing; my diff is pure deletion of never-called methods.
